compute: GPU 3 only, bf16, batch 2 full-encoder updates (~35 GB); ~50 min
question: Does one round of self-training (teacher = fold 4 point specialist; pseudo-points on the 7150 fold-4 training images; student = fresh copy of the fold 4 recipe A encoder) improve held-out point localisation on the 5 validation-green images, and do the student's maps correlate better with GT CD on the fold 4 validation rows than the teacher's?
student_init: experiments/phase2_pooling_20261020/arms/std/runs/fold4/cpdino_vitb/epoch_20.pt (fold 4 recipe A encoder, fold-clean), linear 768->1 head

pseudo_labels.positives: teacher local maxima (+-16 px) with p >= tau_pos; Gaussian sigma 8 px max-target
pseudo_labels.negatives: grid cells whose teacher probability <= tau_neg = 0.10 -> target 0
pseudo_labels.tau_pos_rule: smallest threshold in 0.20..0.95 whose mean in-ROI precision on the 20 train-green images is >= 0.80 (fallback: the most precise threshold); fixed before any validation look
pseudo_labels.flips: four exact flips; points flipped in pixel space, negatives looked up by mapping cell centres back

training: 3000 updates, each batch = 1 strong item (20 train-green x 4 flips, ROI-masked Gaussian BCE) + 1 pseudo item (support-masked BCE), loss = mean of the two; AdamW encoder lr 1e-5, head lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4, clip 1; seed 46

evaluation.primary: val-5 mean F1 at the fixed threshold 0.35 (teacher recomputed in the same code path) ; delta
evaluation.secondary: calibration-free Pearson r between log(feature) and log(GT CD) over the fold 4 validation rows (1790, none leaked) for the phase 0 feature set, teacher vs student
evaluation.information_only: student F1 at other thresholds (never used for selection)

pre_specified_decision: extend to folds 0-3 only if F1 delta >= +0.03 at the fixed threshold and r(log sg_cd_th0.35, log GT CD) is higher for the student than for the teacher
falsification: Student F1 <= teacher F1 + 0.03 means confident-peak pseudo-labels do not add localisation information beyond the 20 strong images at this budget.
known_limits: teacher precision on train-green is optimistic because the teacher trained on them; tau_pos is therefore likely too permissive, which is the conservative direction for the claim
amendment_2026-10-28T15:45Z_before_run: Phase 0 showed grid-quantised features carry no CD signal while the sub-grid spacing estimator (centroid-refined peaks, complete 6-neighbourhoods, CD = 2/(sqrt3 d^2)) reaches r 0.73; the secondary metric is therefore the Pearson r of log sg_cd_th0.35 with log GT CD on the unseen fold-4 validation rows, teacher vs student, instead of the best |r| over all features.
